question.text: Mr. Suresh Menon, an HNI LP in 'Krishna Cat II AIF' (committed INR 5 crore), wants to transfer his commitment to his adult son mid-fund. The Fund's Contribution Agreement permits transfers only with Manager consent, subject to KYC on the transferee. The Manager's MOST appropriate manager-side action is to:

answer.text: Refuse all transfers categorically regardless of agreement terms
Permit transfer subject to completion of KYC/AML checks on the son, execution of adherence deed, and ensuring continued compliance with minimum investment (INR 1 crore) and class-rights
Automatically cancel Mr. Menon's entire commitment

explanation.text: The Logic: The textbook approach: honour the transfer mechanic in the Contribution Agreement, run full KYC on the transferee, require adherence deed to bind the transferee to existing fund terms, and confirm minimums and class rights remain satisfied. The Trap: Option A violates the agreement. Option C fails AML/KYC (XXIV). Option D punishes the LP beyond agreement terms. Cross-Exam Context: XXIV (AML) tests KYC on transfer; XIX-C tests the commercial mechanics of LP transfer. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build a 'transfer fee' into the Contribution Agreement (say 0.25% of commitment) to cover legal/KYC costs — absent this, frequent LP transfers in a large fund eat into the fund admin budget.
